body: Income Tax Act 2007 section BB 1: Income tax is imposed on taxable income at the rate or rates of tax fixed by an annual taxing Act and is payable to the Crown under the Income Tax Act 2007 and Tax Administration Act 1994.

Income Tax Act 2007 section BC 1: The income tax liability of a non-filing taxpayer for a tax year is the total tax withheld from amounts of income included in the taxpayer's annual gross income. The income tax liability of a filing taxpayer is calculated under sections BC 2 to BC 6, with schedular income modifications under BC 7.
Income Tax Act 2007 section BC 2: A person's annual gross income for a tax year is the total of their assessable income that is allocated to the corresponding income year.
Income Tax Act 2007 section BC 3: A person's annual total deduction for a tax year is the total of their deductions that are allocated to the corresponding income year.

Income Tax Act 2007 section BC 4: If annual gross income is more than annual total deduction, the difference is net income. If annual gross income equals annual total deduction, net income is zero. If annual total deduction is more than annual gross income, the difference is net loss and net income is zero. Net loss is included under Part I in the person's tax loss and may be subtracted from future net income, made available to another person, or used in certain other ways.
Income Tax Act 2007 section BC 5: A person's taxable income for a tax year is determined by subtracting any available tax loss that the person has from their net income under Part I.

Income Tax Act 2007 section BC 6: The income tax liability of a filing taxpayer is calculated by multiplying taxable income by the basic tax rate. If the calculated liability is zero or negative, the filing taxpayer's income tax liability is zero. Filing taxpayers with schedular income are determined under BC 7.

Income Tax Act 2007 section BC 7: A person with schedular income has income tax liability equal to schedular income tax liability plus the amount that would be their income tax liability if they had no schedular income. If there is more than 1 kind of schedular income, schedular income tax liability is the total calculated for each kind. Multi-rate PIE rules and natural-person PIE adjustments may modify liability.

Income Tax Act 2007 section BC 8: Credits for tax paid, tax withheld, or other circumstances, calculated under Parts L and M, satisfy a person's income tax liability as far as the credits extend. If income tax liability exceeds total credits, the difference is terminal tax. Remaining credits after liability is satisfied are dealt with under section LA 5.

Income Tax Act 2007 section BD 1: An amount is income if it is income under Part C. Income is exempt income if it is exempt under subpart CW or CZ. Income is excluded income if it is excluded under subpart CX or CZ and is not non-residents' foreign-sourced income. Non-residents' foreign-sourced income is a foreign-sourced amount derived while the person is a non-resident, except specified trustee income. Assessable income is income that is not exempt income, excluded income, or non-residents' foreign-sourced income.
Income Tax Act 2007 section BD 2: An amount is a deduction of a person if they are allowed a deduction for the amount under Part D.
Income Tax Act 2007 section CA 1: An amount is income of a person if it is income under a provision in Part C. An amount is also income of a person if it is income under ordinary concepts.
Income Tax Act 2007 section CA 2: Exempt income is income under subpart CW or CZ. Excluded income is income under subpart CX or CZ and not non-residents' foreign-sourced income.

Income Tax Act 2007 section DA 1: The general permission allows a deduction for expenditure or loss, including depreciation loss, to the extent incurred in deriving assessable income, excluded income, or a combination, or incurred in carrying on a business for the purpose of deriving assessable income, excluded income, or a combination.

Income Tax Act 2007 section DA 2: The general limitations deny deductions to the extent expenditure or loss is capital, private or domestic, incurred in deriving exempt income, incurred in deriving employment income, incurred in deriving specified non-resident passive income, or incurred in deriving non-residents' foreign-sourced income. Each general limitation overrides the general permission.

Income Tax Act 2007 section DA 3: Specific deduction provisions in subparts DB to DZ may supplement the general permission only if they expressly say so. General limitations override supplements unless the supplement expressly states otherwise. Specific provisions may override the general permission or limitations only if they expressly say so. Part E does not supplement or override the general permission or general limitations.
Income Tax Act 2007 section DA 4: The capital limitation does not apply to depreciation loss merely because the item of property is capital in nature.
